listeNoel.modesDesc: The 12 questions are the same in both cases. Together, you each answer for yourself. The quiz tells you which of Santa's lists your couple is on and who is the nicer one.
listeNoel.modeDuoMeta: Your couple's list and who is the nicer one
listeNoel.setupTitreDuo: Have you been naughty or nice this year?
listeNoel.setupDescDuo: Enter your first names. The first person answers the 12 questions and then passes the phone. You each answer for yourself. At the end, you'll know which of Santa's lists your couple is on and who is the nicer one.
listeNoel.setupTitreSolo: Have you been naughty or nice this year?
listeNoel.setupDescSolo: The quiz asks 12 questions about your December, for example about the advent calendar or the hidden presents. Answer with your couple in mind and you'll find out which list Santa has put you on.
listeNoel.duoEgal: It's a tie with {{valeur}} each. Santa puts you on the same list.
listeNoel.ecartsTitre: Where one of you was nicer than the other
listeNoel.invitationDuo: And has your partner been naughty or nice? Take the quiz again together to find out who's bringing the average down.
listeNoel.noteFin: This quiz is a game, just for fun. The real Santa hasn't given us his lists.
listeNoel.modeDuoDesc: You each answer the 12 questions on the same phone, without seeing the other's answers.
listeNoel.modeSolo: On my own, for our couple
listeNoel.modeSoloDesc: You answer with your couple in mind.
listeNoel.relaisDebut: Answer the 12 questions, then pass the phone.
listeNoel.relaisSuite: {{nom}} is done. Your turn, no peeking at their answers!
listeNoel.r1_d: You're right at the bottom of the list. The advent calendar was empty after ten days and the presents were opened early. So Santa has set aside some coal for you this year.
listeNoel.r1_a: The good news is that you make a great match! And with a nice ribbon, a lump of coal can make a pretty decoration.
listeNoel.r2_d: Santa isn't very happy with you this year. He saw the presents bought at the last minute and the boxes shaken early. You make everyone laugh at the table but the elves write down everything you do.
listeNoel.r2_a: All is not lost. One nicely wrapped present and the dishes done together can still save your Christmas.
listeNoel.r3_d: The elves can't make up their minds. One day you leave the last cookie for your partner and the next day you finish the box of chocolates. So your file has been going from one list to the other since the start of the month.
listeNoel.r3_a: You still have a few days to make up for it. Breakfast in bed or doing the dishes without being asked counts double in December!
listeNoel.r4_d: You're on the nice list. You slipped up two or three times, like shaking a box, but nothing that deserves coal. On the whole you look out for each other and Santa has noticed.
listeNoel.r4_a: So Santa will stop at your place. If you want to climb higher on the list, look below at what he wrote down.
listeNoel.r5_d: Santa has nothing to hold against you. You open only one door of the advent calendar a day and your presents have been ready since November. The elves even hold you up as an example in the workshop!
listeNoel.r5_a: Keep it up. You can still get up to a little mischief next year, the elves won't say a word.
listeNoel.q1a: One door a day, not one more
listeNoel.q1b: Two or three doors ahead on rough days
listeNoel.q1d: Empty and the other one's has been started
listeNoel.q2: The presents are hidden somewhere in your home:
listeNoel.q2a: No snooping, the surprise comes first
listeNoel.q2b: No snooping, but the hiding place has been spotted
listeNoel.q2c: A box or two got shaken
listeNoel.q2d: Everything was opened, then neatly rewrapped
listeNoel.q3: The other one's present was bought:
listeNoel.q3a: In November and it's already wrapped
listeNoel.q3c: On the evening of the 23rd, at a run
listeNoel.q3d: On the 24th at 6 pm, at a gas station
listeNoel.q4a: Right down to the last ornament with Christmas music on
listeNoel.q4b: The ornaments, yes. Untangling the lights, no
listeNoel.q4c: Two ornaments hung, then the couch
listeNoel.q4d: Showing up when it's all done to say it's leaning
listeNoel.q5: The box of chocolates from Grandma:
listeNoel.q5a: Just one chocolate when the box goes around
listeNoel.q5b: Two or three, on the way past
listeNoel.q5c: The top layer was gone in one evening
listeNoel.q5d: It's empty and the wrappers are back inside
listeNoel.q6a: Paper, a ribbon and nice sharp folds
listeNoel.q6b: Paper and a lot of tape
listeNoel.q6c: The store bag with a bow on it
listeNoel.q6d: The other one wraps everything and both names are on the tag
listeNoel.q7: You had agreed on $50 per present, tops:
listeNoel.q8a: Clearing the table and serving everyone seconds
listeNoel.q8b: Offering to help while hoping they'll say no
listeNoel.q8c: Staying at the table: someone has to keep them company
listeNoel.q9: Your uncle brings up that touchy subject again:
listeNoel.q9a: Changing the subject while serving dessert
listeNoel.q9b: Staring very closely at the plate
listeNoel.q9c: Slipping in one little remark, just one
listeNoel.q9d: Stirring things up, just to see
listeNoel.q10: The present received is a total miss:
listeNoel.q10a: A big smile and it will get used at least once
listeNoel.q10b: A thank you, then the back of a closet
listeNoel.q10c: Exchanged on the 26th without a word
listeNoel.q11c: Taken, since everyone was told to help themselves
listeNoel.q11d: Eaten in secret in the kitchen
listeNoel.q12a: Little thoughtful gestures all year long
listeNoel.q12b: Good times and two or three slip-ups
